newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil current account hit by trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil current account hit by trade deficit.

text.p: Brazil's $4.6 billion current account deficit in the first two months of 1997 was mainly caused by a deteriorating trade balance but was also influenced by pressures on services, the Central Bank said.
"Clearly it is the result of the trade performance," said the head of the bank's economics department, Altamir Lopes. "Services were also slightly worse," he added.
Brazil posted a trade deficit in January to February this year of just over $2.0 billion compared with a surplus in the first two months of 1996 of $13 million.
The current account gap in Jan-Feb 1996 was $1.9 billion.
The deficit in the services account of the balance of payments was $2.984 billion in January-February compared with $2.501 billion in the same year-ago period.

Lopes said in the two months, external debt servicing fell to $758 million from $1.315 billion a year ago because payments to the Paris Club of debtor nations had been made in December. He said the net shortfall on international trips rose to $639 million from $477 million.
Outflows on repatriated dividends and profits soared in the two months because of the introduction in late January of the new CPMF financial transaction tax, Lopes said.
The deficit there was $844 million in January-February versus only $55 million a year ago.
In January, outflows of dividends and profits were $683 million, reverting to more normal levels of $208 million in February.
Lopes said receipts should increase in March because state-owned Banco do Brasil was expected to repatriate profits.
